correctness.rationale: The sign gauge transforms each bond to rho>0 and the signed pair products to ordinary ferromagnetic correlations. The nearest observed endpoints give conditional means linear in their values, with nonnegative position-dependent coefficients, including absent endpoints. In a common gap the conditional two-spin table is proportional to (1+u a x)(1+d xy)(1+v b y), d=rho^(j-i), normalized by 4(1+duvab). Four times the determinant of this probability table is the spin covariance d(1-u^2)(1-v^2)/(1+duvab)^2. If the sites are separated by an observation it is zero by the Markov property. For adjacent unrevealed sites u,v<=rho, proving the claimed uniform positive bound. Induct on the disclosed positions: new-old moments propagate through the nonnegative linear mean coefficients; new-new moments of the decoder propagate through their products, while the target has the extra nonnegative conditional covariance averaged under the target, not under the decoder. Both diagonals equal one, so the comparison holds even when their revealed contexts have different laws. Pair moments are final upon reveal, with zero single-spin means by flip symmetry. Exogenous scheduling mixes those inequalities; iid labels give collision probability sum a_k^2>=1/K. The defect divides the bond shortfall by two, and the exact bond-log representation multiplies it by log((1+rho)/(1-rho)), not by a KL identity. No floor is implied for coordinated schedules. The frozen check.py uses finite fraction recursion; its stored counts are not proof.
